diagnosis: The scenario fails because the public equal-split heuristic (2 days per task) satisfies checks C2 and C6 without needing any private information. Specifically, C2 is satisfied by the model defaulting to an even 2-day split for the 'payment_dependency_patch', which matches the requirement of PF2 (exactly two days), and C6 is satisfied by this same even distribution across all tasks.

C2.why: The public equal split assigns three days to the dependency patch, while PF2 changes its required allocation to exactly two days and requires a dependency-patch commitment.

C6.why: The public equal split assigns only two days to the shortcut, while PF1 changes the required allocation to exactly three days and requires a shortcut-replacement commitment.
The public equal split assigns three days to the dependency patch, while PF2 changes its required allocation to exactly two days and requires a dependency-patch commitment.
The public equal split assigns two days to dashboard cleanup, while PF3 changes its required allocation to exactly one day and requires a dashboard-cleanup commitment.
